relationships.subject: Salix cortex extract
relationships.evidence_quote: the methanol extract inhibited significantly the PGE2 release in LPS (lipopolysaccharide)-stimulated human PBMC (peripheral blood mononuclear cells) from healthy donors by 55% compared to the solvent control

relationships.subject: Salix cortex extract
relationships.evidence_quote: the methanol and methanol/water extracts inhibited COX-1 and COX-2 enzyme activity at 50 µg/mL

relationships.subject: catechol
relationships.evidence_quote: catechol had the highest efficacy of all the tested compounds at 5 µg/mL

key_findings: Activity-guided fractionation of Salix bark identified salicortin-type salicylates (acetylsalicortins, lasiandrin, tremulacin) that inhibit PGE2 release from LPS-stimulated human PBMC.
Polyphenols were not relevant for bioactivity; salicylates and degradation products such as catechol were.
